metadata.title: Why You Can't Check an AI Watermark.
metadata.purpose: Answer one real question in the Plain register: how do you check a watermark detector? Lands the carry-out that a detection is an attestation, not a proof.
metadata.anchor_pair: S03 -> S14 (must be the SAME composition)
metadata.one_flag: S11 — the only hedge in the reel

skin_warnings: B00: palette=claude but the cold open is 'un-annotated' — COLD OPEN LAW wants ClaudeComposerAsk

beats.narration_text: Someone asked how you check whether a watermark detector is telling the truth. Turns out you can't. Liam. Take them through it.

shot.new_visual_element: Shannon puppet, lab, speaks to camera, hands off

beats.note: Audio baked into media/B00.mp4 by Seedance (voice MARCUS). No mp3 for this beat.

beats.narration_text: A detector says AI wrote this. There is no way for you to check that.

production_viz.label: Verdict card, no way in
production_viz.mechanic: A verdict card reading DETECTED on cream. A viewer's hand reaches toward it and meets a flat boundary — no seam, no panel to open.

beats.narration_text: Not for you, not for a university, not for a court — only the company that made the watermark can run the real test.

production_viz.label: Three locked out, one inside
production_viz.mechanic: Three labelled figures outside a closed boundary: YOU, UNIVERSITY, COURT. One figure inside: the provider. Only the inside figure holds the key.

beats.narration_text: Hold on to one case: a student's paper, flagged, and a committee that has to decide something.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ANCHOR — flagged paper, empty table

production_viz.label: THE ANCHOR — flagged paper, empty table
production_viz.mechanic: THE ANCHOR. A paper on cream with a terracotta FLAGGED stamp, beside an empty committee table. THIS EXACT COMPOSITION RETURNS AT S14.

beats.narration_text: The natural assumption is that a watermark is a signature — maths anyone can verify, the way your browser checks a website's certificate.

shot.new_visual_element: The signature model — the wrong guess

production_viz.label: The signature model — the wrong guess
production_viz.mechanic: A padlock and certificate; a green tick appears that several onlookers can all see at once. Sell the signature model as reasonable.

beats.narration_text: Here's the tell: the same company shipped both, in the same announcement — images got the open signature anybody can check, and text got a secret key and a promise of an API later.

production_viz.label: Same announcement, two trust models
production_viz.mechanic: Split panel from one announcement: LEFT an image with an open standard badge and a public tick; RIGHT a block of text with a sealed key and a dotted 'API — later' placeholder.

beats.narration_text: If text watermarks were signatures, they would have used a signature.

shot.new_visual_element: Only one side has a tick

production_viz.label: Only one side has a tick
production_viz.mechanic: The same two panels held; the public tick exists on one side only. Nothing else moves.

beats.narration_text: The reason is that the watermark's key does two jobs at once.

production_viz.label: One key, two jobs
production_viz.mechanic: One key in the centre, two arrows leaving it: WRITE and READ.

beats.narration_text: It decides which words get quietly nudged during writing — and reading the mark means re-running that same key over the text and counting.

shot.new_visual_element: Write with it, read with it

production_viz.label: Write with it, read with it
production_viz.mechanic: The key seeds a nudge pattern across a sentence being written; then the identical key sweeps back across the finished text, tallying matches.

beats.narration_text: So the key that detects is the key that forges: publish it, and anyone can fake the mark or scrub it off.

production_viz.label: Publish it and it breaks
production_viz.mechanic: The key is published; two outcomes branch immediately — text that fakes the mark, and text with the mark stripped.

beats.narration_text: Which is why it stays secret, and why the only party who can run the test is the party being asked to vouch for itself.

production_viz.label: The tester is the vouched-for
production_viz.mechanic: The key seals back inside the provider boundary. The tester and the vouched-for are drawn as the same shape.

beats.narration_text: One flag — a black-box detector is a deployment choice, not a law of the maths; nothing stops a provider from publishing a verifier, and some designs are built to be checked in the open.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ONE FLAG — two possible futures

production_viz.label: THE ONE FLAG — two possible futures
production_viz.mechanic: Two futures side by side: a sealed detector, and a published verifier anyone runs locally. A single terracotta FLAG marker over the beat — the reel's only hedge, labelled as one.

beats.narration_text: Researchers have shown you can learn a lot about a secret watermark just by poking at it from outside — enough to imitate it, or strip it.

production_viz.label: Probing infers the shape
production_viz.mechanic: Probes strike a sealed box from outside; its internal shape fills in as a dotted outline. The key itself stays blank — structure inferred, secret not recovered.

beats.narration_text: Which leaves the worst of both: secret enough that an honest outsider can't check the verdict, not secret enough to stop someone attacking it.

shot.new_visual_element: Secret both too much and too little

production_viz.label: Secret both too much and too little
production_viz.mechanic: The box with two figures: the honest checker stopped at the wall; the attacker passing through the dotted outline.

beats.narration_text: So back to the committee: they can't check it, the student can't check it, and the appeal is to a company's word about its own product.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ANCHOR RETURNS — a verdict on letterhead

production_viz.label: THE ANCHOR RETURNS — a verdict on letterhead
production_viz.mechanic: THE S03 COMPOSITION RETURNS, identical — flagged paper, same table. The only change: the verdict is now a letterhead, signed.

beats.narration_text: A detection doesn't prove the maths held — you're trusting that the right key, the right version, and the right threshold were used on that exact text.

production_viz.label: Detected, and four blanks beneath
production_viz.mechanic: DETECTED at the top; four unverifiable assumptions listed beneath it, each with an empty checkbox nobody can tick.

beats.narration_text: And no detection doesn't mean no AI — another company's key is invisible to this one, by design.

shot.new_visual_element: Not detected, and a key unread

production_viz.label: Not detected, and a key unread
production_viz.mechanic: NOT DETECTED at the top; a second key sits beside the reader, unread, greyed. Mirrors S15's construction.

beats.narration_text: You can't check a watermark. You can only ask the company that made it, and believe the answer.

props.quote: You can't check a watermark. You can only ask the company that made it, and believe the answer.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Here's the prompt — read it with me. Take a claim you'd have to act on: a plagiarism flag, a fraud score, a risk rating. Write down who runs the test, who holds the inputs, and what exactly a second party could recompute on their own. Then mark every line you'd have to take on trust. Most systems people treat as verdicts turn out, on that list, to be attestations. Liam, in for Bear.
